cards.text: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, just went to war alongside Ahab, king of Israel, and Ahab didn't make it home (2 Chronicles 18:28-34). Jehoshaphat did. He's back in Jerusalem, safe.
He's home, and who goes out to confront him? Jehu son of Hanani the seer (not King Jehu of Israel), and friend, that man did NOT bring a welcome-home cookie box.

cards.question: Jehu goes out to confront King Jehoshaphat. What does Jehu call him out for?
Because Jehoshaphat helped the wicked and loved those who hate the LORD, Jehu says the ___ of the LORD is upon him.
Jehu tells Jehoshaphat that some good is found in him too.
What good does Jehu say Jehoshaphat has done in the land?

answers.text: He fed the hungry in Judah

cards.text: Jehu adds that Jehoshaphat has set his heart on seeking God. That's your boss saying "We need to talk" and then "Also, GREAT work this year" in the same meeting.
Jehoshaphat lives in Jerusalem, and once again he goes out among the people, from Beersheba all the way to the hill country of Ephraim.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat goes out among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim. What does he do there?

answers.text: He turns the people back to God
He collects taxes for the palace

cards.text: Next he appoints judges in each of the fortified cities of Judah. Then he gives them a word: consider carefully what you do.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat reminds the new judges whom they are really judging for. It's the ___.
Jehoshaphat tells the judges the LORD is with them when they judge, and may the fear of the LORD be upon them. Why does he tell them to be careful?

answers.text: With the LORD there is no partiality or bribery
The LORD will remove any judge who turns aside
The LORD keeps a record of every judgment

cards.text: Nobody's slipping the judge a cookie box under the table, not even one of mine, and baker, mine are GOOD. Then Jehoshaphat appoints judges in Jerusalem too, to judge on behalf of the LORD and settle disputes.

cards.question: In Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat appoints some of the Levites, ___ and heads of the Israelite families to judge on behalf of the LORD.

cards.text: He charges them to serve faithfully and wholeheartedly in the fear of the LORD. Every dispute from their brothers in the cities comes to THEM, and friend, that's being the one person everybody tags in the group chat when there's an argument.

cards.question: When a dispute comes from their brothers in the cities, Jehoshaphat tells the Jerusalem judges to send it on to the king.
Jehoshaphat tells the Jerusalem judges to warn the people who bring disputes, so that they will not incur ___ before the LORD.
Jehoshaphat puts two men over the Jerusalem judges: Amariah the chief priest and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah. Who is over all that pertains to the LORD?

cards.text: Zebadiah is over all that pertains to the king, and the Levites will serve as officers before the judges.
Then Jehoshaphat sends them off with this: "Act resolutely; may the LORD be with the upright!" We'll leave King Jehoshaphat right there for now, friend, but his story is still in the oven.
